newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ says agrees with union on cuts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ says agrees with union on cuts.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd said on Wednesday that it had agreed with the Finance Sector Union (FSU) that staff cuts should be carried out through natural attrition.

ANZ chairman Charles Goode told the bank's annual meeting that staff reductions would be necessary due to the changing face of banking, which is moving away from traditional branch networks towards electronic delivered services.

"Some of the areas we would agree with are that what change or lost staff are necessary or eventuate from the restructuring, should be by attrition," he said in response to a question from FSU shareholder, Tony Beck, who is also joint national secretary of the FSU.
"We are also putting more emphasis on retraining," Goode said.
Goode declined to go any further on the sensitive issue of staff cuts, which has already seen workers walk off the job.
He referred the question to managing director Don Mercer, saying the issue should be taken up in negotiations with the union.
Beck told the meeting that the ANZ bank was now the only bank in Australia not to have reached an agreement with the FSU on the way the restructuring for the bank industry would be carried out.
"This is the only bank where we are encountering so many difficulties in reaching a sensitive understanding in the way this reform will proceed," Beck said.
